title: Local Conversion: U.S. Southwest And Ontario
summary: Compare how global compute, industrial, housing, and infrastructure signals encounter named utility, water, workforce, permitting, construction, and delivery systems in Arizona and Ontario.
current_state_summary: The two local dossiers now contain named system and project records, but neither supports a readiness conclusion: Arizona adds TSMC's serving utility and a regional workforce node to its service, wastewater, permit, and construction stack; Ontario adds a current Toronto construction-stage baseline to its planning, infrastructure, pipeline, and application records.
current_state: In the Southwest, SRP's E-67 tariff defines service conditions and Project Huckleberry records online infrastructure for one named Meta project.
APS identifies TSMC in its service territory and NNME Southwest identifies a 47-member workforce node, while customer capacity and delivered workforce outcomes remain unresolved.

The Phoenix AMA Fifth Management Plan adds effective industrial conservation, measurement, reporting, and compliance requirements without resolving a named project's allocation, service, use, or reuse outcome.
Phoenix records a Fab 3 topping-out milestone and a metropolitan workforce baseline while facility-level capacity and workforce outcomes remain unresolved.
In Ontario, IESO and Toronto Hydro records establish planning layers rather than project capacity.
CMHC's June 2026 Toronto CMA data separates approved-but-not-started units, active construction, completions, and starts without supplying a matched project-conversion rate.
Toronto's development pipeline, building-permit release, and water capital plan expose the distance between intention, approval, servicing, construction, and completion.
Application 24 254930 remains date-gated for a post-Council recheck; no later stage is inferred before the official record changes.

dependency_stack.current_state: Data-centre demand, semiconductor investment, housing targets, and infrastructure forecasts establish pressure on receiving systems.
dependency_stack.boundary: Broad demand and policy records do not establish a local site's feasibility, capacity, timing, or outcome.

dependency_stack.current_state: SRP tariff, APS service territory, Arizona regulatory rails, IESO outlook, Toronto Hydro proceeding, and municipal plans make authority and conditions visible.
dependency_stack.boundary: Serving-utility identity, rules, and system plans do not prove that a specific customer or development has a connection, service commitment, or spare capacity.

dependency_stack.current_state: Project Huckleberry, TSMC Fab 3, and Toronto application 24 254930 create specific trails that can be followed over time.
dependency_stack.boundary: One serviced project does not transfer to another; topping out is not operation; planning recommendation is not enacted approval or delivery.

dependency_stack.current_state: The record includes one online electrical project, a structural fab milestone, a regional workforce node, and current citywide and metropolitan development-stage baselines.
dependency_stack.boundary: The dossiers lack complete facility utility, permit, workforce-outcome, supplier, project-finance, matched conversion, construction, completion, and occupancy evidence.

dependency_stack.current_state: No current pathway record supports corridor-wide industrial readiness or successful housing delivery from the selected application.
dependency_stack.boundary: Outcome claims require measured service, operation, production, employment, completion, occupancy, affordability, and community evidence.

evidence_limits: The Southwest and Ontario are compared as receiving systems, not treated as equivalent markets, institutions, or project types.
The pathway does not infer TSMC electric capacity from Meta's Project Huckleberry or industrial water capacity from municipal drinking-water compliance.
APS's TSMC service-territory statement is not a customer service agreement, and NNME Southwest's membership is not a workforce-outcome measure.
The Phoenix AMA Fifth Management Plan is an area-wide regulatory layer, not evidence of a named site's water allocation, provider capacity, service commitment, actual use, or compliance.
Toronto's citywide pipeline and capital plans do not prove that application 24 254930 will receive enacted amendments, permits, financing, construction, completion, or occupancy.
CMHC's approved-not-started stock, under-construction stock, completions, and starts use different timing bases and cannot be converted into a matched project rate.
Workforce surveys and training cohorts do not establish semiconductor hiring sufficiency, retention, contractor capacity, or program outcomes.
The Toronto Council and DARPA Lift Challenge records remain governed by their dated recheck rules.
next_records: After July 31, Toronto Council disposition, bills and by-laws, condition compliance, land and laneway actions, building permits, starts, completions, and occupancy for application 24 254930.
TSMC-specific electric-service, load, infrastructure, energization, water, wastewater, reclaimed-water, permit, inspection, occupancy, equipment, qualification, and production records.
Facility classification, annual water-use reporting, provider, right, variance, audit, inspection, and compliance records that connect Phoenix AMA requirements to named industrial sites.
NNME Southwest agreements, funded training delivery, completions, placement, retention, vacancies, supplier and contractor demand, and facility-level operating-employment evidence.
Toronto project-level feeder, transformer, water, wastewater, servicing, financing, construction-labor, cancellation, completion, and occupancy records.
